amos.6.p1.b1.text: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Mount Samaria, the distinguished ones of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.

amos.6.p1.b2.text: You lie on beds inlaid with ivory, and lounge upon your couches. … You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph.

amos.6.p1.b3.text: Therefore, you will now go into exile as the first of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will come to an end.

amos.6.p1.b4.text: “Silence,” … “for the name of the LORD must not be invoked.”

amos.6.p1.b5.text: “Do horses gallop on the cliffs? Does one plow the sea with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison …

amos.6.p1.b6.text: ‘Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?’

amos.6.p1.b7.text: I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,” … “and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.”
